adjudications.adjudication: Reject as an established material source defect; retain transcript-only detail as a disclosed residual dependency and strengthen primary corroboration where already available.
adjudications.exact_current_excerpt: Management’s December-quarter outlook is a 7–10% total-revenue increase, 8–9% Services growth, 45–46% gross margin and $20.4–20.8 billion operating expenses. The directly retrieved transcript attributes constrained shipments to supply and Services headwinds to third-party licensing and FX. It also identifies price increases, carry-in inventory and cheaper non-memory components as partial offsets to memory inflation; carry-in benefits diminish while memory prices are expected to rise further. These are management statements in a **third-party transcript**, not an independently transcribed issuer recording. [S15]
reasoning: The complete directly retrieved Motley Fool transcript includes named speakers and the precise cited quarterly guidance, licensing/FX headwinds and memory/inventory offset remarks. No contradiction or misattribution was found in the local original.

The current memo explicitly identifies third-party transcription and lack of independently transcribed issuer audio; its annual forecast remains a house assumption. A categorical issuer-primary-only rule does not follow merely from the importance of a correctly attributed secondary source. If the governing task separately requires primary-only claims, that external rule would change admissibility, but the reviewer has not identified such a rule or an actual erroneous remark.

The original issuer 10-K independently supports current component supply constraints and expected intensification of memory/storage cost pressure. It also supports general bundled-service revenue deferral. Exact quarterly guidance, licensing/FX and carry-in-offset detail remain transcript-dependent; primary corroboration should not be overstated.

The review lists detailed cloud-cost accounting among memo claims, but the current memo body contains no assertion that Siri AI cloud costs are recognized in Services cost of sales. Its AI paragraph instead says inference margins are not established. That part of the allegation is broader than the current text.

primary_evidence.exact_text: The Company is experiencing supply constraints and rising costs driven by industry-wide supply-demand imbalances for key components, including advanced semiconductors, memory and storage. The Company expects these trends to intensify for memory and storage components.

The Company allocates revenue and any related discounts to all of its performance obligations based on their relative SSPs. Because the Company lacks observable prices for product-related bundled services, the allocation of revenue is based on the Company’s estimated SSPs. Revenue allocated to the delivered hardware and bundled software is recognized when control has transferred to the customer, which generally occurs when the product is shipped. Revenue allocated to product-related bundled services is deferred and recognized on a straight-line basis over the estimated period they are expected to be provided.

transcript_evidence.exact_text: We expect our December quarter total company revenue to grow between 7% and 10% year-over-year, which reflects our best view of constrained supply.
We expect services revenue to grow between 8% and 9% year-over-year in the December quarter. This contemplates sequential headwinds, primarily driven by third-party licensing and foreign exchange.

We also expect to see some benefit from carry-in inventory in the December quarter as well, as well as lower costs on certain non-memory components. And looking beyond the December quarter, we see the pricing for memory purchases continuing to increase.

adjudications.proposed_clarification: The issuer filing independently confirms component constraints and rising memory/storage costs. The precise quarterly guide and licensing/FX and carry-in-inventory commentary below come from management statements in the retrieved third-party transcript; they have not been reconciled to issuer audio. [S4, S15]

adjudications.proposed_replacement: The numerical Products path is a house assumption. Management’s pricing/mix offsets and Morningstar’s general 2028 margin-recovery view motivate testing recovery, but neither supplies or validates this specific Products gross-margin path. [S15, S29]

adjudications.adjudication: Reject as a substantive historical-data contradiction; accept explicit future-evidence wording.
adjudications.exact_current_excerpt: FY2027 category revenue growth at least 12%, with disclosed pricing/mix or shipment evidence supporting persistence; a single quarter is insufficient. The conditional path uses 13%, 10%, 8.5%, 7% underlying growth for its first four years, then base.
reasoning: This is a prospective review condition dated2027-11-15, not a claim that the packet already contains a historical units-times-ASP bridge. The memo explicitly says observations trigger investigation and do not establish the entire decade.

Qualitative disclosed pricing/mix commentary can exist without a full quantitative units-times-ASP bridge: the original10-K attributes FY26iPhone growth to Pro models and management transcript discusses product price increases and constraints. Shipment/unit precision may still be unavailable.

The strongest clarification is to say that the threshold requires new evidence and to allow qualitative evidence without inventing a shipment series. Unavailable evidence should prevent automatic adoption rather than force a made-up bridge.

source_evidence.exact_text: iPhone net sales increased during 2026 compared to 2025 due to higher net sales of Pro models.

adjudications.proposed_threshold: FY2027 category revenue growth at least 12%, with new issuer disclosures or other substantiated evidence on demand, supply normalization, pricing or product mix that supports persistence. Such future evidence may remain unavailable; the condition does not assume a disclosed historical units-times-ASP bridge, and a single quarter is insufficient. The conditional path uses 13%, 10%, 8.5%, 7% underlying growth for its first four years, then base.

tax_source_points.adjudication: A stronger preference rationale is warranted, but FY2024 headline24.1% is distorted by an explicitly identified one-time provision charge and does not by itself refute a17% forward expense-rate anchor. Cash-tax normalization remains a house judgment.
tax_source_points.exact_current_excerpt: The filing reports $34.588 billion of cash income taxes paid, or 21.72% of $159.237 billion consolidated pretax income. That is a cash-paid/profit ratio, not a measured unlevered operating tax rate: settlement timing and nonoperating items differ. The full provision-to-cash reconciliation is not modeled. Cash operating tax is normalized at 17% in all cases, supported as an expense-rate anchor by the latest effective rate and management’s quarterly guidance rather than claimed to equal cash paid. The $34.588 billion cash payment also exceeds the $27.062 billion income-tax provision by $7.526 billion; the packet does not allocate that difference to specific settlements or timing effects. The debt tax shield uses a separate 25% normalized marginal-rate **house assumption**. The former matches the latest effective-rate anchor but is not proven permanent; the latter is not asserted to be Apple’s reported tax rate. Uniform 20%/24% operating-tax stresses reduce weighted value to $160.33/$152.25, holding other inputs fixed. [S4; computed diagnostics]
